gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: Only in an emergency ___ this exit be used.
gaps.explanation: may + be + participle: this exit may be used only in an emergency.

gaps.sentence: So convinced ___ he of his innocence that he refused the deal.
gaps.explanation: 'So convinced was he of …' — inversion after fronted 'so + adj'.

gaps.sentence: At no point ___ the passengers instructed to stay seated.
gaps.explanation: 'At no point were the passengers instructed …' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
gaps.explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ anyone realise how close the firm was to insolvency.
gaps.explanation: "Little did anyone realise" = nobody realised — emphatic inversion with do-support.

gaps.sentence: Only when the results were published ___ the scale of the error become clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Only when … did the scale … become clear' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
gaps.explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.
